name: Production Distro RC5
source: TASK.md; RC4 final audit; operator-hosted mirror request
goal: Stand up a controlled hosted mirror service framework for aios.w33d.xyz, then prove hosted metadata verification and canary-readiness without weakening RC4 authority boundaries.
core_thesis: AIOS becomes more distributable by exposing signed, hash-bound release metadata through a minimal hosted mirror while all signing, activation, rollout, and rollback authority remains outside the static mirror service.
non_goals: Do not claim GA production readiness.
Do not store or read private production signing material on the mirror service.
Do not host large release payloads in RC5; only service framework, metadata, placeholders, and small indexes are in scope.
Do not let nginx, static files, shell, TUI, model replay, or remote service code activate a release or mutate active slots.
Do not treat DNS or HTTP reachability as release proof without hash binding, freshness, rollback, and fail-closed evidence.
primary_acceptance: The hosted mirror service contract defines endpoint layout, storage boundaries, nginx boundary, metadata freshness, and fail-closed behavior for aios.w33d.xyz.
The remote service framework exposes health and channel metadata without private keys, activation authority, or large artifact storage.
Local verifier evidence proves hosted endpoint availability and rejects missing, stale, tampered, or oversized metadata.
Distributable channel projection explains how a user can fetch AIOS release metadata and bootstrap artifacts while preserving RC4 signing and promotion gates.
Multi-node canary proof remains exact-approval gated and rollback-ready; no production ring mutation is allowed by default.
